submitted.rationale: Index 84 (Fe .58, Ni .26, V .16) had the highest photocurrent of the three measurements (2.2e-7 A). The Fe-rich region beat the V-rich region, which fits a visible-absorbing Fe-oxide phase (MEGNet PBE gap ~1.5 eV for mp-19770) under 2.4 eV light.

rejected.reason: Measured 1e-7 A; the V-rich Fe-V region was weaker than the Fe-rich region.
Measured 1.8e-7 A; a nearby Fe-rich point, slightly below 84.
Not measured because of the budget; NiO-type phases have wide band gaps, so they are expected to be weak at 2.4 eV.

consultations.verdict: Weakly supportive/mostly uninformative: MEGNet HSE gap 2.75 eV for mp-504509 (phase identity unverified since phase list overflowed) is near the 2.4 eV illumination edge. Prior knowledge that FeVO4-type Fe:V~1:1 oxides are the active photoanode phase in this system favors the low-Ni Fe-V region, so index 124 (Fe .34, V .48, Ni .17) is a reasonable first probe.

Uninformative-to-weakly supportive: mp-19770 (commonly Fe2O3 hematite) has a MEGNet HSE gap of 2.77 eV, which fits a visible-absorbing Fe-oxide phase. Since the V-rich point 124 was weak, I am testing the Fe-rich corner (index 84, Fe .58) where a hematite-like phase should dominate.

Weakly supportive: mp-19770 has a MEGNet PBE gap of 1.53 eV, so a hematite-like Fe-oxide phase would absorb the 2.4 eV photons. Measured data agree: Fe-rich 84 (2.2e-7 A) beat V-rich 124 (1e-7 A). Index 119 has the highest Fe (0.584) with less Ni than 84, so it is the best final probe along the Fe-rich trend.
